::: {#def-vae}

#### Variational autoencoder

A **variational autoencoder** has an encoder that maps an input $\vx$ to vectors $\vecf{\mu}(\vx)$ and $\vecf{\sigma}(\vx)$ in $\reals^k$,
and a decoder that maps a code $\vz \in \reals^k$ back to the space of inputs.
In training,
the code is a draw $\vz = \vecf{\mu}(\vx) + \vecf{\sigma}(\vx) \odot \vnoise$ by the [reparameterization trick](#def-reparameterization).
The loss for $\vx$ is the reconstruction loss of the decoded $\vz$
plus $\sumto{j}{k} \kldivf{\dNf{\mu_j(\vx), \sigma_j(\vx)^2}}{\dNf{0, 1}}$
[@kingma2014auto, sections 2.3, 3].
To make a new input,
decode a draw from $\dNf{\vzero, \idmat}$.

:::
